subject: Traffic-sampler + MAP unit-econ sanity check
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@stately.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Traffic-sampler + MAP unit-econ sanity check

Oliver — attaching a draft MAP and a small traffic sample you shared earlier. Wanted to get ahead of the common unit-econ questions before our evaluation kickoff next week. Short summary up front:

- Goal: validate tokens/$ assumptions in the MAP under realistic bursty traffic and with prefix/KV caching and batching enabled.
- Deliverables attached: MAP-v0.3.xlsx (milestones & gating criteria), stately-traffic-sample.csv (your sample), and a short runbook for a microburst sim.

Key assumptions I used in the draft MAP (please confirm or correct):
- Model baseline: open-large-1 (64-bit float) equivalent token price used for planning: $0.000015 per token (i.e. ~66.6k tokens per $1).
- Request profile: avg prompt 120 tokens, avg generation 320 tokens (total ~440 tokens/req).
- Expected production mix: 70% short lookups (<= 120 tokens), 25% medium (300–600 tokens), 5% long (>900 tokens).
- Initial cache hit-rate scenarios: 0%, 40%, 70% (we'll test these in sim).
- Default continuous-batching target: batch size 4–8 depending on concurrency; we model both 4 and 8.

Asks from you before we run the sim:
1) Confirm the traffic sample is representative (I used the file you dropped in Drive).
2) Any constraints on latency SLO we must respect? I used 200ms p95 as the MAP gate.

Planned MAP gating for unit economics (draft):
- Gate A (pilot): end-to-end tokens/$ within 20% of modeled target at 40% cache hit and batch size 4, p95 latency <= 200ms.
- Gate B (close): tokens/$ within 10% at sustained 30-day traffic profile, cache hit >= 50% observed, no SLA breaches >1%.

Next steps: if you confirm the traffic and latency target, we'll run a week-long microburst sim (synthetic microburst + real traffic mix) and return a short results package and an updated MAP with recommended batch/caching config.

Thanks — looking forward.

—
Jordan Blake

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Traffic-sampler + MAP unit-econ sanity check

Thanks Jordan — this looks good. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Traffic: the CSV is a 72-hour extract from production (timezone PST). It includes several short daily spikes (10–15 reqs/sec lasting 30–90s) and one larger hourly microburst (120 reqs/sec for 2–4s). The long-request percentage you used is fine (we have a small set of long-form transcription jobs).

2) Latency: our product team is targeting p95 <= 250ms initially; 200ms would be ideal but is aggressive for the first pilot. If you can show that the 250ms gate hits unit-econ targets we can accept.

3) Cost target: we don't have a hard floor but we'd like to see tokens/$ for steady-state walk to be <= $0.015 per 1k tokens (i.e., <= $15 per million tokens) after caching and batching. If that's doable in the pilot, great; otherwise we need a clear path in the MAP to get there.

I've attached an annotated sample with two days highlighted (heavy microburst day + normal). Let us know if you need additional telemetry (concurrency histograms or per-endpoint size distributions).

Oliver

Kim / Ben — forwarding Oliver's note and the sample. Can we run a microburst sim with the following matrix this week and capture tokens-per-$ across scenarios?

Matrix (each test = 1 simulated day):
- Cache hit rates: 0%, 40%, 70%
- Batch sizes: 1 (no batch), 4, 8
- Two latency gates: p95 250ms and p95 200ms
- Model variants: open-large-1 (baseline), open-quant-8 (8-bit quantized)

Specific asks:
- Ben: can you run the sim and produce per-scenario tokens/$, p95 latency, and CPU/GPU utilization? Add heatmap visuals if possible.
- Kim: can you validate whether the MAP gate definitions are acceptable from the onboarding/ops side? I set Gate A/B in the MAP (attached) as discussed.

Timeline: get synthetic sim results by Tue 2026-06-01; consolidate and draft recommended MAP adjustments by Wed 2026-06-02 so we can send an update to Stately.

Thanks — Jordan

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Traffic-sampler + MAP unit-econ sanity check — sim results (summary)

Quick run of the microburst sim completed. High-level summary first, then attachments with full tables/heatmaps.

Summary (baseline = open-large-1, batch=1, cache=0%):
- Baseline tokens/req: 440 tokens average (matches Jordan). Baseline tokens/$ = ~66,667 tokens per $1 (using $0.000015/token).
- Scenario A (cache 40%, batch 4): tokens/$ improves ~18–24% depending on model quantization. p95 latency median of runs = 230ms (meets the 250ms gate, close to 200ms).
- Scenario B (cache 70%, batch 8): tokens/$ improves ~35–42% (strong wins), but p95 shifts to ~260–290ms in the heaviest microbursts for batch=8. Quantized model reduces p95 by ~10–15% vs float and improves tokens/$ by additional ~12%.
- Tradeoffs: batch size 8 gives the best tokens/$ but risks breaching 250ms p95 during the 2–4s microbursts. Batch=4 is the pragmatic sweet spot for the pilot.

Operational notes:
- A small prefix/KV cache for common prompts improves tokens/$ quickly — we see the largest delta from 0%->40%. 70% is achievable only if Stately pushes templated prompts to the cache (their success rate for short lookups will determine this).
- We modeled steady-state and microburst arrival patterns; prefetch (warming) during expected peak windows reduces the p95 delta on batch=8, but requires coordination in the MAP (a scheduled warm-up or prefetch job).

Deliverables attached: microburst-sim-results-20260531.pdf (charts), sim-raw-output.csv, recommended-MAP-adjustments.txt

Bottom line recommendation for MAP pilot: set Gate A to require batch=4 default + an operational prefetch plan for known burst windows. Use quantized model variant for pilot to preserve latency and improve tokens/$.

—

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: MAP update: Pilot configuration & timeline (tokens/$ focus)

Oliver — thanks for the sample and context; Ben and Kim ran the microburst sim and we updated the MAP with concrete pilot config and gates. TL;DR: the target you asked for (~$15 /M tokens) is reachable in the pilot with the following plan.

Pilot configuration we recommend (what Redwood will deliver):
- Model: open-quant-8 (quantized) as the default pilot model.
- Batching: default continuous-batching with target batch size = 4; dynamic bump to 6 during warm windows if prefetch enabled.
- Caching: prefix/KV cache enabled. MAP includes a short integration step where Stately will seed the top 200 prompt templates into cache prior to pilot start.
- Warm-up: scheduled prefetch job 60s before expected large microbursts (we'll coordinate windows).

Gating criteria (updated in MAP v0.4):
- Gate A (pilot acceptance): tokens/$ <= $15 per M tokens (measured across the 7-day sim window), observed cache hit >= 35% and p95 <= 250ms.
- Gate B (close): tokens/$ <= $14 per M tokens sustained over 30 days, cache hit >= 50%, p95 <= 220ms.

Proposed MAP timeline (milestones):
- 2026-06-04: pilot kick-off (deploy pilot config, seed cache).
- 2026-06-04 -> 2026-06-11: evaluation window (7 days) + telemetry collection.
- 2026-06-12: joint readout, Gate A decision.
- 2026-06-26: final close / commercial sign-off if Gate B met or path accepted.

Action items for Stately:
- Oliver: confirm the 250ms p95 acceptance for Gate A (we can keep 200ms as stretch but defaulting to 250ms aligns expectations).
- Send list of top 200 prompt templates to seed cache (CSV) by EOD 2026-06-03.

I've attached MAP-v0.4 (with updated gates & timeline) and Ben's sim PDF. If you sign off on the 250ms Gate A, we'll schedule the kickoff for 2026-06-04 and start the evaluation window.

Thanks — Jordan
